newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BONDS SET FOR GENTLE FALLS IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BONDS SET FOR GENTLE FALLS IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose minimally in early trade on Friday but dealers foresaw a moderately falling trend in a quiet market, with ongoing jitters about a possible German repo rate hike next week.
"There are no key U.S. data until next week, so it's going to be calm. There is still a certain nervousness about the German repo rate," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.03 point from Thursday's close at 112.58, yielding 6.06 percent. The seven percent 2007 bond, due to be be benchmark on September 1, was up 0.02 point at 105.47, with the yield at 6.25 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged from Thursday night's 58 basis points.
The crown traded at 3.8095 to the mark at 0735 GMT, down a tad from 3.8085.
